# Joint rotations and common full section centroids

This extends `candidate 5e600a897e2488c6`. Its extremal and finite-facet
hypotheses remain in force. It does NOT assume transverse cap cuts.

## 1. Admissible continuous-normal variations

Keep each positive circuit weight vector rho_i fixed, but now allow its
continuous normals u_ij to vary subject to

    sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0.

At the original family, u_ij is nonzero and its matrix has rank k_i-1.
Both properties persist under sufficiently small perturbations in this
linear constraint space: a nonzero (k_i-1)-minor stays nonzero, while the
fixed dependence keeps the rank at most k_i-1. The same fixed positive rho
therefore remains a minimal positive circuit. The vectors need not retain
unit length after variation; they have unit length at the differentiation
point.

The projected coverage constraints

    sum_j rho_ij(v_ij.p-b_ij)>=0

are unchanged and remain linear. With the continuous dependence imposed,
they still guarantee that each assigned fiber is covered. Thus these
normal variations are valid even for rank-deficient circuits, without
pretending that arbitrary unconstrained rotations preserve them.

## 2. Boundary coincidences require subdensity moments

At a facet contained in a cap boundary, the relative normal displacement
under a joint perturbation is affine in the continuous point x on that
facet. It can change sign WITHIN the facet. The first variation is therefore
an integral of a minimum or maximum of affine functions, not a constant
fraction of the whole facet.

The correct generalized gradient uses a measurable trace theta_F(x) in
[0,1] on each such facet. Its effective cap-section measure is

    (1-theta_F) H_(d-1)|F     if the original body lies inside the cap,
    theta_F H_(d-1)|F         if the body lies outside the cap.

On a transverse section use its ordinary H_(d-1) measure. On a strictly
empty or strictly full fiber with no boundary coincidence, the section
measure is zero. Denote the effective section measures by nu_ijz.

The SAME trace supplies the body-facet term theta_F times facet area in
the shape derivative. The cap-parameter part is

    delta v_ij . sum_z z nu_ijz(R^d)
      + delta u_ij . sum_z integral x dnu_ijz
      - delta b_ij   sum_z nu_ijz(R^d).

This follows directly from the relative swept-prism formula. The two
linear branches at each x select theta equal to zero or one; their convex
hull permits values in [0,1]. Keeping the same theta in every term is
necessary for the identities below.

Only the total mass and first moment of theta_F H_(d-1)|F enter these
finite-dimensional parameter derivatives. Their admissible set is compact
and convex. One elementary compactness proof is to take a weakly convergent
subsequence of the finite measures theta_l H_(d-1)|F on the compact facet.
The limiting measure is still dominated by H_(d-1)|F, as is seen by testing
against nonnegative continuous functions, and therefore has a density theta
between zero and one. Mass and first moments converge. This proves
compactness of the required finite-dimensional moment set.

## 3. Separation still supplies normalized multipliers

For each active cap, its generalized gradient set is compact and convex in
the finite-dimensional support/cap-parameter space. The actual directional
derivative is bounded above by its support function. Common erosion belongs
to the admissible tangent cone and has a uniformly strictly negative pairing
with EVERY gradient in every active cap set: the fixed positive boundary
patch lying in the open cap contributes a strict loss, and all coincident
trace contributions are nonpositive. Rotating-normal coordinates are zero
in this direction.

The separation argument from the finite-gradient proof remains valid.
For completeness, the relevant cone is closed: write it as the nonnegative
cone generated by the compact union of active cap-gradient sets, plus the
polar of the polyhedral admissible tangent cone. Pairing a convergent
sequence in this sum with the common strict-decrease direction bounds its
total cap-generator coefficient. Compactness then gives convergence of the
cap part, and the remaining polar part converges in its closed cone. If the
volume gradient were outside this closed cone, separation and a small
addition of common erosion would produce a feasible volume-increasing
perturbation, a contradiction.

Thus one obtains the same nonnegative lambda_ij and eta_ip, and now also a
vector multiplier for each equation sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0. The chosen gradients
use admissible measurable traces exactly as in Section 2. Caratheodory in
the finite parameter space can express each selected gradient using finitely
many gradient moment vectors; no numerical or infinite-dimensional
stationarity assertion is being substituted here.

## 4. All cap sections in a stressed group have one full centroid

Write

    S_ij=sum_z nu_ijz(R^d),
    Z_ij=sum_z z nu_ijz(R^d),
    X_ij=sum_z integral x dnu_ijz.

The threshold and integer-normal equations remain

    lambda_ij S_ij = rho_ij t_i,
    lambda_ij Z_ij = rho_ij sum_p eta_ip p,
    t_i=sum_p eta_ip.

Continuous-normal stationarity gives a vector q_i, common to the group,
with

    lambda_ij X_ij = rho_ij q_i.

Therefore every cap in a nonzero group has the SAME full effective section
centroid

    (Z_ij/S_ij, X_ij/S_ij)
      = (bar_z_i, bar_x_i)
      = (sum_p eta_ip p/t_i, q_i/t_i).

All effective section measures are positive measures supported on the
original cap sections inside C. Their common centroid therefore belongs
to C and to every cap boundary in the group. The identity
sum lambda_ij=1/beta still follows from the joint homothety and is unaffected
by the variable traces or rotations.

## 5. Exactly when this centroid is the transported deepest-point apex

Choose globally deepest centers (p,x_p) at the integer indices carrying
eta_ip. As proved in the compressed-stress note, every such center lies on
every cap plane of its assigned group. Hence

    y_i^deep=sum_p (eta_ip/t_i)(p,x_p)

belongs to C and to all these planes, and has the same integer coordinate
bar_z_i as the common section centroid. It follows exactly that

    bar_x_i - sum_p eta_ip x_p/t_i
       belongs to intersection_j ker(u_ij).

For a full-rank circuit k_i=d+1, that kernel is zero. The common FULL section
centroid then equals the convex combination of globally deepest mixed-
integer centers, so it has ambient depth exactly beta. This equality is
proved, not inferred from matching only integer marginal barycenters.

For k_i<d+1 the conclusion is only equality modulo the stated common
continuous kernel. The common section centroid still lies in C and on all
group cap planes, but no claim that it lies in the convex hull of the chosen
deepest points is justified by these equations alone.

Allowing rho itself to vary does not supply additional geometric freedom.
If rho changes to a nearby positive rho-prime, replace its cap coefficients
(u-prime,v-prime,b-prime) by (rho-prime/rho) times those coefficients. The
cap halfspace is unchanged, the original fixed-rho continuous dependence
holds, and every projected coverage expression is unchanged. Thus these
variations are already represented in the fixed-rho linear parameterization.
Equivalently, the formal rho-stationarity equations reduce to the common-
plane identities: their nonconstant part is proportional to
b_ij-v_ij.bar_z_i-u_ij.bar_x_i, which is zero, and the normalization multiplier
is zero. The reparameterization proves this without assuming a constraint
qualification for a new bilinear (rho,u,v,b) parameter system.

No estimate of the per-group multiplier sum is proved in this note.
